learning_outcomes.text: Understand and manage the basic concepts, properties, and results of complex variables, numerical and function series, Laplace transform, first and second-order differential equations and systems, and partial differential equations.
Model processes and systems to solve them with differential equations.
Understand and use the concept of approximation and know the usual methods of numerical calculation.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to differential equations, definitions, notations.
Methods for solving ordinary differential equations.
Linear first-order differential equations, trajectories and examples.
Linear higher-order differential equations with constant coefficients.
Linearization of systems, solutions, examples and modeling.
Numerical series, function series, convergence and examples.
Classical examples: Heat, wave, and Laplace equations.
Numerical calculation and approximation of solutions.

assessment_methods.method: Written evaluation (covering all topics if no partial pass)

assessment_rules: The course is passed if a final grade equal to or greater than 5 points is obtained. The final grade (NF) is calculated as 0.8 * E + 0.2 * Pr, where E is the written evaluation grade and Pr is the practical activities grade. Practical activities (Pr) account for 20% of the final grade and are not recoverable. The written evaluation (E) accounts for 80% and can be taken as a partial exam (E1) on Topics 1-4 (60% of E) and a final exam (E2) on Topics 5-6 (40% of E). To pass E1, a minimum of 5 points is required; if passed, the grade is kept. If E1 is passed, E2 must also be passed with at least 5 points; if E2 < 5, the grade is not specified. If E1 is not passed, a comprehensive final exam must be taken, requiring a minimum of 4 points in each of its two parts (Part 1 and Part 2) to pass; otherwise, the written evaluation grade (E) will be a maximum of 4 points.
